title: Dal Tadka
subtitle: Indian yellow lentil dal with a spiced butter finish
excerpt: Dal tadka is one of the most common dishes served across Indian households and roadside dhabas. Soft lentils are cooked until tender and then finished with a hot spiced oil poured over the top. The sizzle and fragrance of the tadka is what sets it apart.
sourceNotes: Dal tadka is eaten from Kashmir to Kerala, though the spices and lentil variety shift by region. The tadka technique -- blooming spices in hot fat and pouring it over cooked food -- is one of the most fundamental methods in Indian cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the dal without the tadka. Reheat gently and make a fresh tadka to finish.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the lentil base easily. Make the tadka fresh each time.

content.text: Red lentils (masoor dal) work in place of green if that is what you have. They cook faster and produce a smoother, thicker texture. The tadka is poured on at the very end and stirred in just before serving, so keep the heat ready.

items.prepNote: use 6 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed

content.text: Put the lentils in a large saucepan with 900ml of water. Bring to the boil, skimming off any foam. Add the turmeric, then reduce the heat to a steady simmer.
Cook the lentils uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes until completely soft and beginning to break down. Stir occasionally.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a frying pan. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes to the onion pan. Cook for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Pour the tomato mixture into the cooked lentils. Add salt. Stir and simmer together for 5 minutes. Adjust consistency with hot water if needed.
Make the tadka: heat the remaining oil in the small pan until very hot. Add cumin seeds, cardamom pods, and chilli flakes. Fry for 30 seconds until fragrant and sizzling.
Pour the hot tadka straight over the dal. Stir through the coriander. Serve immediately with rice or roti.

items.cause: Old lentils or hard water can slow cooking
items.fix: Add more hot water and continue simmering, covered, for another 10 minutes

items.cause: Not enough salt, or the tadka was not hot enough
items.fix: Season carefully and make sure the oil is smoking before adding the spices to the tadka
Stir in 100ml of hot water and simmer briefly to loosen

content.text: Dal tadka is the backbone of North Indian cooking. It is served at roadside dhabas, in home kitchens, and at weddings alike. The word tadka means tempering -- the technique of blooming spices in hot fat. Every region has its own version, but the idea of finishing with a sizzling oil is constant.
